title: High‐flux polycaffeic acid‐PVDF composite membrane for selective antibiotic desalination
content:
Abstract

The recovery of antibiotics from saline wastewater presents a significant challenge in water treatment. While polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) ultrafiltration membranes offer excellent chemical and mechanical stability, their application in this domain is restricted by intrinsic large pore sizes and insufficient hydrophilicity, leading to poor selectivity and limited water flux. Here, we report that a highly permeable and selective composite membrane was achieved via the surface polymerization of caffeic acid. Aided by H2O2 and Cu2+, this modification deposits a robust polycaffeic acid (PCA) layer that simultaneously narrows the membrane pores, enhances hydrophilicity, and establishes a strong negative surface charge across a broad pH range. Governed by electrostatic interactions, the PCA-PVDF membrane demonstrates highly efficient and selective antibiotic desalination, achieving a high water flux of 1941.7 L m−2 h−1 bar−1. It rejects over 90% of cationic or amphoteric antibiotics while allowing more than 80% permeation through neutral or negatively charged antibiotics and salts. Exhibiting high operational stability for antibiotics such as tetracycline and ciprofloxacin, this strategy provides a scalable pathway for designing selective membranes for complex organic-saline separations.
